rationale: A offers an attractive end-to-end code path, but as written the code would not run. It tokenizes with cl100k_base (a vocabulary of about 100k) while building the model with vocab_size=50257, so embedding lookups fail. Its target slice is one token longer than the input, causing a shape mismatch. 'device' is never defined, and it lists a model checkpoint (gpt-neox-20b) as a dataset. For a step-by-step guide aimed at a Python beginner, these errors seriously undercut its main advantage. B is less code-heavy but more complete and pedagogically sound. It builds up from neural-network basics, implements BPE from scratch (truly 'from scratch'), and explains embeddings, attention, FFN and residuals with milestones. It covers training considerations and hardware, notes masking the instruction tokens in SFT, and adds KV caching, sampling and serving. It ends with a graded project roadmap and modern upgrades (RoPE, RMSNorm, GQA). B has minor slips, such as a muddled sinusoidal-versus-learned phrasing and a dubious course reference, but none break the learner's path.
